adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — When external update succeeds, the helper never deletes an existing local recovery credential, so codes from before a rotation remain valid through local fallback.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the createRecoveryCodesCredential method in CredentialHelper.java (lines 112-129), when userStorageCreated is true (external storage update succeeds), the method only logs and returns. It never removes any existing local credential. The code path shows: if updateCredential returns true, it logs success and exits; otherwise it creates in local storage. There's no cleanup of existing local credentials when external storage is used. This means if a user previously had recovery codes stored locally and then rotates them with external storage, the old local codes would still exist and potentially be valid through the fallback mechanism shown in RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential which checks federated first, then falls back to local storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80 — A separate read after isValid can observe stale external state and miss allCodesUsed, leaving the user without a required action after consuming the final code.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a race condition between isValid and a separate read that could miss allCodesUsed. Looking at the diff for RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java, the only change is on line 80 where getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream is replaced with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(). This change is about where to look for credentials (federated vs local storage), not about the timing between isValid and reading allCodesUsed. The finding references a race condition issue that isn't introduced or exposed by this diff - the same potential timing issue would exist before and after this change.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — The test provider accepts every generated code and never removes one, so the new happy-path test silently passes while recovery codes are reusable indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java, the isValid method for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE (lines 283-302) only checks if the input code exists in the stored list using `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` but never removes the used code from storage. This means recovery codes can be reused indefinitely in the test provider. While this is a test provider (not production code), it means the test doesn't properly validate the one-time-use behavior of recovery codes, which is a legitimate test coverage concern for the new functionality being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — A successful user-storage update leaves any prior local recovery credential intact, so its old recovery codes remain valid through the local validator after migration.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the createRecoveryCodesCredential method in CredentialHelper.java (lines 112-134), when userStorageCreated is true (user storage successfully updated the credential), the method returns without removing any existing local credential. The code only creates a local credential via recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential when userStorageCreated is false. This means if a user previously had recovery codes stored locally and then migrates to user storage, the old local recovery codes would remain valid since there's no cleanup of the local credential after successful user storage creation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — The SPI implementation validates recovery codes without consuming the matched code, allowing the same supposedly single-use code to authenticate repeatedly.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() at line 283-305, the recovery code validation only checks if the code exists in the list (generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))) but never removes or marks the code as used. However, this is test code in a testsuite provider (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage), not production code. The test storage is designed for backwards compatibility testing, not for implementing full security semantics. While technically accurate, this is test infrastructure code where simplified behavior is acceptable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:86 — removeStoredCredentialById only targets Keycloak storage, so it cannot remove the exhausted credential returned by an external CredentialInputUpdater.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() now checks federated credentials first (getFederatedCredentialsStream()), meaning credentials can come from external user storage. However, in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java around line 86 (not shown in diff but referenced), the code uses removeStoredCredentialById which only removes from Keycloak's local storage. If the credential came from an external CredentialInputUpdater (federated storage), removeStoredCredentialById won't be able to remove it, leaving exhausted recovery codes in place. This is a real bug in the credential lifecycle management.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — Successful validation never consumes the matched recovery code, allowing the same supposedly single-use code to authenticate repeatedly.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the isValid method in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java around line 340, the code validates recovery codes by checking if the input matches any code in the stored list: `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()));`. However, after successful validation, the matched code is never removed from the stored list. This means the same recovery code can be used multiple times for authentication, which defeats the purpose of single-use recovery codes. The code reads the credential data, validates against it, but never updates/removes the used code from storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:115 — Accepting both a credential model and an independent raw-code list exposes two representations that can drift, so creation should cross this boundary as one typed request.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real design concern in the new createRecoveryCodesCredential method at line 115. The method accepts both a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel and a separate List<String> generatedCodes. Looking at the implementation, the generatedCodes list is serialized to JSON and used for userStorage update, while the credentialModel is used for local storage creation. This creates two separate representations of the same data that could potentially drift. However, this is an architectural/design concern rather than a bug - the code will function correctly as written. It's a valid code review observation about API design that could lead to maintenance issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:238 — Recovery-code JSON is decoded again at line 334 with raw `List.class`, duplicating parsing while discarding the element type; centralize a typed decoder.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that JSON parsing with raw `List.class` occurs at both line 238 (in getCredentials) and line 334 (in isValid) in the BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java file. Both use `JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class)` without type parameters, which loses type safety. This is a valid code quality concern about duplicated parsing logic that could be centralized, though it's not a bug since the code will function correctly. The finding is grounded in actual code visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:19 — A missing federated credential is unconditionally unwrapped, so an inconsistent or transiently unavailable user-storage record turns recovery-code login rendering into a 500 instead of a controlled authentication failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java, the code was changed from `user.credentialManager().getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst().get()` to `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` which returns an Optional, but then immediately calls `.get()` on line 19 without checking if the Optional is present. If the credential is not found (either in federated storage or local storage), this will throw a NoSuchElementException, causing a 500 error instead of a controlled authentication failure. The finding correctly identifies that an unconditional unwrap of the Optional can cause a server error when the credential is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — Successful federation updates do not delete an existing local recovery-code credential, so superseded recovery codes remain valid.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the createRecoveryCodesCredential method in CredentialHelper.java (lines 112-134), when userStorageCreated is true (meaning the credential was successfully stored in user storage), the method simply logs and returns. It does not delete any existing local recovery-code credential. If a user previously had recovery codes stored locally and then the federation storage is updated, the old local credentials would remain valid. This is a security issue where superseded recovery codes could still be used for authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:262 — Retry the same recovery code and assert rejection, because the sole happy-path login does not detect that the new federated validator leaves every recovery code reusable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points out that the test only verifies a happy-path login with recovery codes but doesn't test that used codes are invalidated. Looking at the diff, the BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() method at line 283-305 simply checks if the input code exists in the stored list (generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))) but never removes or marks the code as used. The test at line 237-270 only performs a single login with recovery codes without verifying that the same code cannot be reused. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added functionality - the federated validator implementation appears to leave codes reusable, and the test doesn't catch this.
